design: fixed finite bank of independent all-null Gaussian candidates; no adaptive data reuse
spending_rule: alpha / (r * (r + 1)), r starts at 1; no renormalization
limitations: Synthetic random-intercept paired differences only; not LLM or financial empirical evidence.
Each candidate has a fresh independent Gaussian sample; no shared baseline error, validation-data reuse, adaptive proposals, heterogeneous cluster sizes or non-Gaussian robustness.
All effects are zero; reported rejection means any false promotion within the fixed candidate prefix, not predictive performance or power.
Equal-size independent clusters make the cluster-mean t test exactly calibrated under this Gaussian null; this does not prove robustness in general settings.
Budgets are nested prefixes of one bank; methods and budgets are dependent and intervals are pointwise Monte Carlo intervals, not simultaneous uncertainty bounds.
Alpha spending spends alpha*K/(K+1) over K candidates, so its lower rate is not a power or superiority finding.
The design was fixed before this run, but was researcher-authored after seeing prior baseline results; not external preregistration.
